senses.gloss:
Bhṛṅgin
(‘One [who assumed the form of a bhṛṅga or a] beetle’)
------------------------------------------
According to an account in the Kālikāpurāṇa (chapter 45) भृङ्गिन् along with महाकाल, was a door keeper at शिव’s place as also a general of his troops. But other accounts in the पुराणस् describe him as a sage who was devoted only to शिव and looked down upon पार्वती, शिव’s spouse. At पार्वती’s request to ‘teach him a lesson’ शिव assumed the Ardhanārīśvara form. When भृङ्गिन् arrived at कैलास to pay his obeisance to शिव which included pradakṣiṇā or circumambulation also, he is said to have become a ‘bhṛṅga’ or a beetle, and bored a hole in the middle so that he could go round शिव only to the exclusion of पार्वती! Hence the name भृङ्गिन्. When पार्वती cursed him to become weak and emaciated, शिव, out of compassion, endowed him with a third leg, so that he could complete the circumambu-lation.
This story though it appears as funny, may symbolically represent the attempts of uniting the Śaiva and the शाक्त cults which might have been at loggerheads at one time.
In iconographical representations भृङ्गिन् is shown as a ṛṣi or a sage with three legs, an emaciated body and a face resembling that of an ape. He is sometimes classed among the bhairavas.
See also ARDHANĀRĪŚVARA and BHAIRAVA.
